- The EZ Work Permit Website & User Manual is available at https://ezwp.wda.gov.tw/wcfonline/wSite/Control?function=IndexPage. [1]
- The Student Account / Password Login.pdf is also available at https://oia.ncu.edu.tw/static/file/26/1026/img/389/std20230311_010101.pdf. [1]

- The maximum fine for a student who works without a work permit is NT$15, and the permit can be revoked if the employer fails to apply or fails to work. [5]
- The work permit can be applied online via the EZ Work Permit Website (https://ezwp.wda.gov.tw/), which is managed by the Labor Ministry. [5]
- The application can be submitted by email to the Labor Ministry office; the permit can be revoked by the employer if the employer fails to apply or fails to work. [5]
- The introduction process of receiving work permits can be found in Chapter 7 Receive the Electronic Document. [1]

- The extension period is based on the validity period of the proof of enrollment (not exceeding six (6) months) [2]
- A total extension period cannot exceed two (2) years [2]

- The 1990 hotline for foreigners in Taiwan is called 1990 [1]
- It is also referred to as 業務諮詢一覽表 (1990 外來人士在臺生活諮詢服務熱線) [1]

- If an employer does not enroll a student worker in labor insurance, they may be fined 4× the labor insurance fee and 10× the employment insurance fee for the period the employer fails to enroll. [1]
- If the employer fails to enroll a student worker in labor insurance, they may be fined 4× the labor insurance fee and 10× the employment insurance fee for the period the employer fails to enroll. [5]

- A bachelor's degree takes four years and at least 128 credits in total. [1]
- Your department may require more; its curriculum table has the exact number. [1]
- Contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- 12 additional graduation credits are required for overseas students admitted on an equivalent qualification; military training and PE do not count toward these. [1]
- Courses from other departments that are approved to count as general education fill your general-education electives first; only credits beyond that count as electives from other departments. [5]

- At least 16 credits each semester in the first, second, and third academic years [1]
- At least 9 credits each semester in the fourth academic year [1]

- International students must take the full‑year five‑credit course "Chinese for Overseas Chinese Students" (僑生國文) [1]
- They are not required to take the Chinese (B): Chinese Writing course [1]
- For more information, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw [1]

- Take 6 credits of Mandarin courses at the Language Center instead of the freshman Chinese. [1]
- File for the Chinese course substitution before you graduate. [1]
- Contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- Students are required to take five physical education courses in five semesters (Freshman PE I, Freshman PE II, and three PE interest electives) [1]
- These courses carry no graduation credits [1]
- After completing the five semesters, students may take an additional 1‑credit PE course, which also does not count toward graduation [1]
- For more information, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw [1]

- A master's degree requires at least 24 credits, not counting thesis credits. [1]
- You must take at least one graduate course of 1 credit or more at NCU; waived courses do not count. [1]

- Students admitted directly into a doctoral program must complete at least 34 credits, including at least 18 doctoral-level credits. [1]
- The credit count does not include dissertation credits. [1]
- For more information, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- Apply before the add/drop deadline of your first semester; the application will be reviewed individually. [1]
- If approved, you will skip both semesters of Freshman English and receive 6 credits that count toward graduation. [1]
- For more information, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- Undergraduates need at least 100 service hours on the NCU passport before they can receive the degree certificate. [1]
- Check your hours on the Service Learning Website or in the Graduation System. [1]
- If you fail to complete the minimum of 100 service hours, you will not be able to receive the degree certificate. [1]
- For questions, contact the Center for Service Learning, Office of Student Affairs (學務處服務學習發展中心) at https://service-learning.ncu.edu.tw/. [1]

- Service learning is not listed among the graduation conditions for master's and doctoral students. [1]
- The graduation conditions are completing all required courses and credits, passing the degree examination, and receiving satisfactory conduct grades each semester. [1]
- Individual departments may set additional requirements. [1]
- For more information, contact the Center for Service Learning, Office of Student Affairs (學務處服務學習發展中心) at https://service-learning.ncu.edu.tw/. [1]

- The service-learning course is required for two semesters, with different course numbers. [2]
- The course does not count toward the number of credits for graduation. [2]
- For more details, see the service-learning rules. [2]

- IELTS: 5.5 (admitted 115 or later) [2]
- Linguaskill LR: 145 (admitted 114 or earlier) or 150 (admitted 115 or later) [2]
- BESTEP: 聽說讀寫總分 700，且聽力 90、閱讀 90、口說 260、寫作 260 [2]

- TOEIC LR: 600 (admitted 110 or later) [1]
- TOEFL ITP: 483 (admitted 110 or later) [1]
- TOEFL IBT: 64 (2026-01-21 新制成績為 3.5 級) (admitted 110 or later) [1]
- IELTS: 5.0 (admitted 110 or later) [1]
- Linguaskill LR: 145 (admitted 114 or earlier) or 150 (admitted 115 or later) [1]

- The program requires an English proficiency certificate at CEFR B1 (Threshold) or above. [1]
- Example scores include TOEFL iBT: 42; IELTS: 4; TOEIC: 550; GEPT: Intermediate. [1]
- Applicants from an English‑speaking country are exempt from providing an English proficiency certificate. [1]
- The English proficiency test comparison chart and list of English‑speaking countries can be found at https://cis.ncu.edu.tw/AdmissionSys/oia/activity?type=1. [1]

- The Ph.D. in Institute of Network Learning Technology (網路學習科技研究所博士班) is offered by the College of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (資電學院) [1]
- The program is taught in English (sufficient) and requires a total of 24 credits, including 24 elective credits and 0 required credits [1]
- The program duration is 4 years [1]
- Regulations can be found at https://www.lst.ncu.edu.tw/NLT_new/page.php?slug=method&lang=en [1]
- Mon-Fri 9:00-17:00 (Taipei time, UTC+8) [2]

- The IIPP Program handles visiting student programs (IIPP, TEEP) [4]
- The TEEP Program is an international internship program offered by the National Science and Technology Council (NSTC) to provide high‑quality internship opportunities in Taiwan for emerging global research talent [4]

- Take bus 132 or 133 from any campus stop towards Zhongli; the ride takes about 20–30 minutes. [1]
- Bus 132 ends at Zhongli Bus Station, a short walk from the train station. [1]

- Students receive a monthly internship allowance of NT$30,000, provided by the check disbursement method. [3]
- The disbursement timing depends on the date of the IIPP funds credited. [3]
- For more information, contact Ms. Kelly Chien, Tel: 03-422-7151 Ext. 57080. [3]
- Eligible nationalities: Vietnam, Indonesia, Philippines, Thailand [1]
- The application period for the INTENSE Program is from October 1 to October 22, 2026 [1]

- Bring your student ID or passport/visa/ARC (only for first-time applicants) [2]

- The fee for the Taiwan Area Residence Certificate for a Hong Kong or Macau student applying for the first time is NT$1,000. [4]
- The entry-exit permit fee for a Hong Kong or Macau student is NT$1,000. [4]

- You must enroll in the National Health Insurance (NHI) if you have lived in Taiwan for 6 months or more, or if you have been absent for 1 year and not exceeding 30 days. [3]
- You can enroll on the day you start employment, with no waiting period. [3]
- You can enroll on the day you start work, with no waiting period. [3]
- If you are employed, you can enroll on the day you start work, with no waiting period. [3]

- Mainland Chinese students who are eligible for National Health Insurance should pay TWD 4,956. [1]
- Those who are not eligible should pay TWD 3,000 to extend coverage provided by Cathay Life. [1]
- Application period: July 6th to July 20th, 12:00 PM, 2026. [1]

- 畢業後可申請以「其他」事由延期居留1年，可再申請一次，總延期居留效期最長可達2年。 [1]
- 取得工作許可後，可儘速變更為工作居留。 [1]
- 若未及時變更居留原因，原居留證將被廢止，可能面臨逾期罰鍰或限期出境。 [1]

- 至少要修滿二十四學分（不含論文學分）[1]

- 學士班學生須完成中大護照 100 基本時數，否則無法領取學位證書。 [1]
- 可於【服務學習網】或【畢業審核系統】查詢。 [1]

- 每年學期為 109-110 年自行負擔560 元。 [2]
- 僑生若未住滿6個月之僑生，可自費參加國泰人壽醫療保險，一學期為 3,000 元。 [2]

- 每月保費為 1,377 元，若自付6成（826元），政府為4成（551元）。 [1]
- 申請資格為在學僑生取得居留證後在臺居留滿6個月，且期間不得出境超過30天，出境次數以1次為限。 [1]
- 健保費計算方式為新臺幣4494元/6個月，含在學雜費內一次繳清，若有清寒證明，僑務委員會將補助新臺幣375元/月，補助後費用為新臺幣2244元/6個月。 [1]
- 申請人必須於入學後一個月內完成清寒證明報到國際處承辦人，並由僑務委員會審核通過後方能辦理補助。 [1]
